items.title: An idempotent modulo an ideal is lifted by an etale ring map that is an isomorphism modulo the ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma is the second of the two lifting examples of the section: given a ring A, an ideal I and an idempotent ebar in A/I, there is an etale ring map A to A' inducing an isomorphism A/I to A'/IA' and carrying an idempotent e' lifting ebar (statement lines 1784-1789). The proof is a 12-line explicit construction (proof lines 1792-1803): it chooses any lift x of ebar, forms the ring A' obtained from A[t]/(t^2 - t) by inverting the element t - 1 + x, checks that A to A' is etale because the derivative 2t - 1 satisfies (2t - 1)^2 = 1 and so is invertible, identifies A'/IA' with A/I[t]/(t^2 - t) inverted at t - 1 + ebar, and shows that the map sending t to ebar is an isomorphism, which also proves that the class of t in A' is an idempotent lifting ebar. The construction of A' and the etale computation are both carried out in full; the only step a reader has to follow is the identification of the quotient of A' by IA' with the quotient of the polynomial ring.
